subtitle: Lesson 18 · Zero Trust for Data and Applications

eyebrow: A static API key is a flat network, at the app layer

steps.label: Long-lived
steps.sub: often valid for months, from any network location

steps.label: All-or-nothing
steps.sub: leaked key = full service privilege, indefinitely

steps.label: Shared secret
steps.sub: no cryptographic proof of who's really calling

eyebrow: Mutual TLS — both sides prove identity
caption: Ordinary TLS proves only the server's identity; mTLS requires proof from both ends.

eyebrow: Sidecar handles it, app code never sees a key
code:
[ App container ]
      |
[ Sidecar proxy ] <-- mTLS handshake,
      |                 cert rotation,
      v                 mesh policy
[ Network / other services ]
caption: The service mesh sidecar is the policy enforcement point — identical concept to Chapter 1, applied at the service layer.

eyebrow: What proves identity vs. what proves authorization

steps.label: Short-lived token
steps.sub: proves WHAT it's allowed to do, expires in minutes

steps.label: Leaked token
steps.sub: already close to useless by the time it's exploited

subtitle: Replacing long-lived pipeline secrets with federated, short-lived credentials.
